Ford recently announced 800 job cuts in the UK and criticized the government for rules requiring car companies to sell more electric vehicles each year. Ford had previously supported these rules in 2022, calling for even higher targets to signal a transition to electric cars. However, the slowing demand for electric cars has led to a shift in the industry, prompting Ford to now deem the ZEV mandate as "unworkable".

Female electric cars had been on the rise, but the pandemic changed the game for carmakers. With low interest rates and high demand, car manufacturers struggled to keep up with production. Now, as demand for electric cars slows down, Ford and other car companies are facing challenges in meeting the ZEV mandate targets set by the government.

P.P.S Any other questions?.
